title: Clutch or Coincidence? Testing Gujarat Titans’s Pressure-Performance Narratives
dek: Is Gujarat Titans' record in tight finishes a skill or a coincidence? Two statistical tests, one on their own record and one on the whole league, give the answer.
excerpt: Gujarat Titans have won more than half their close matches. Across the league, a side's close-match record in one season barely predicts the next, which is the clearest test of whether clutch is real.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: The Clutch Narrative
body: Every franchise has a story about how it handles pressure. The statistical question is whether those stories describe a repeatable skill or a run of coin tosses that went one way.
Gujarat Titans have won {{ev:cc-close-won}} of {{ev:cc-close-n}} close matches, {{ev:cc-close-pct}}, with a ninety-five per cent interval of {{ev:cc-close-ci}}.

sections.heading: Test One: Their Own Record
body: If each close match were a coin toss, a record at least this far from even would occur with probability {{ev:cc-close-p}}. Across the league, the number of franchises whose record differs from a coin toss at the conventional threshold is {{ev:cc-close-sig}}.
Gujarat Titans' record does not pass the first test.

sections.heading: Test Two: Does It Persist?
body: A real skill should carry over from season to season. Across {{ev:cc-n}} franchise season pairs, close-match win rate in one season correlates with the next at {{ev:cc-r}}.
There is almost no persistence: last season's close-match record says little about this season's.

sections.heading: Why Clutch Is So Hard to Find
body: Close matches are decided by a handful of deliveries, so even a genuine edge is buried in noise. Squads also change from season to season.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Coincidence
body: On both tests, close-match records look like chance.
Gujarat Titans should judge pressure performance on process, such as death bowling and wickets in hand, rather than on close-match results.

hypotheses.statement: Hypothesis: individual players' strike rates in the final two overs of close chases persist more from season to season than team close-match records do.
hypotheses.whyUnverified: Player-level clutch persistence has not been measured.
hypotheses.howToTest: Correlate each batter's final-two-over strike rate in close chases across consecutive seasons.

methodology: Built from the CricField warehouse (Cricsheet ball-by-ball data, regulation innings). Models are fitted on the warehouse itself and described in full here. Generated by scripts/editorial/engine. Close = decided by ten runs or fewer, six balls or fewer to spare, or a super over. Persistence uses franchise-seasons with at least three close matches in consecutive seasons.
